reply: t is modulated by x (the bare cos/sin terms plus x·cos/x·sin terms), on top of a polynomial in x and v. Adding a second frequency, a decaying envelope, v-modulation or a phase shift on x or v did not close the gap, so the true x or v dependence is probably non-polynomial in a way I did not identify.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, x, v, params):
    p=params
    w=0.3505
    c=np.cos(w*t); s=np.sin(w*t)
    return (p[0]+p[1]*x+p[2]*v+p[3]*x**2+p[4]*x**3+p[9]*x*v
            +c*(p[5]+p[6]*x)+s*(p[7]+p[8]*x))
